    #Part (b)

    For rate of change of pressure to be zero, cosθ=0 such that ∇T⋅u=0.
    Thus, the unit vectors for which rate of change is zero are perpendicular to ∇T.

    dtdT​=(23,5,41−2e2)⋅(a,b,c)

    dtdT​=23a+5b+(41−2e2)c

    0=23a+5b+(41−2e2)c

    Any unit vector that satisfies the above equation gives the
    direction in which the rate of change of pressure is zero.

    #Part (c)

    For rate of change of pressure to be maximum, cosθ=1.

    dtdT​=∇T⋅u

    dtdT​=∣∇T∣∣u∣cosθ

    Since ∣u∣=1 and cosθ=1,

    dtdT​=∣∇T∣

    dtdT​=232+52+(41−2e2)2​

    dtdT​=35.236

    #Question 3

    #Part (a)

    Let a=(x,y,z).
    Let b=(p,q,r).
    Let c=(s,t,u).

    Since each vector is the cross product of the other two vectors,
    we can infer that a, b, and c are perpendicular to each other
    (arranged in a similar fashion to the x-, y-, and z-axis).

    #Part (b)

    Expressing ds in terms of dt,

    ds=(dtdx​)2+(dtdy​)2+(dtdz​)2​ dt

    ds=(1+b)2+(2t)2+(b−2)2​ dt

    ds=1+2b+b2+4t2+b2−2b+4​ dt

    ds=4t2+2b2+5​ dt

    Substituting start point into parametric equations,

    t+bt=2+2b

    t(1+b)=2(1+b)

    t=2

    Substituting end point into parametric equations,

    t+bt=4+4b

    t(1+b)=4(1+b)

    t=4

    Thus, integration is from t=2 to t=4.

    ∫ 3x−2y​+z ds

    =∫24​ 2t(2b−1)4t2+2b2+5​ dt

    Let u=4t2+2b2+5.

    du=8t dt

    4du​=2t dt

    ∫24​ 2t(2b−1)4t2+2b2+5​ dt

    =41​∫24​ u​ du

    =41​[3/2u3/2​]24​

    =61​[(4t2+2b2+5)3/2]24​

    =61​[(2b2+69)3/2−(2b2+21)3/2]
